text: Next point: which codename would you give to the whole Faro project? One line, no thinking.

summary:
**Summary**

ana asked AllIn to settle 23 points, each with a proposal and reasoning. AllIn answered each in the same structure: a proposal, its main reason, two rejected alternatives (keep current → monthly time cost; bigger rewrite → 3+ weeks, blocks other work), the decision, and a standing open item (ownership to be decided by ana at the Thursday meeting, recorded in project notes; revisit before next release, not mid-release).

Decisions 1–16:
1. Staging server: port 9940 on box "lince" (only box with 64 GB).
2. Database: PostgreSQL 17, one schema per client (row-level security too slow).
3. Login flow: magic links, 15-min expiry (clients forget passwords).
4. Error logging: JSON lines, daily rotation, 30-day retention (old syslog lost stack traces).
5. Release calendar: every second Thursday (Mondays clash with support).
6. Backups: nightly to NAS "tejón", weekly offsite (last restore took 6 h).
7. API versioning: /v2 prefix, v1 frozen until March (two clients still on v1).
8. Mobile app: PWA, no native app this year (budget 40 000 €).
9. Search: PostgreSQL full-text search first (Elasticsearch needs another box).
10. Invoices: PDF via WeasyPrint, numbered per year (accountant's request).
11. Support inbox: one shared inbox with tags, no ticket tool (only two answer).
12. Load testing: k6, 500 virtual users before each release (March outage hit at 300).
13. Translations: Spanish + Catalan now, English later (most clients in Girona).
14. Design system: plain CSS variables, no framework (old Bootstrap theme caused conflicts).
15. Monitoring: Uptime Kuma, 1-min ping (last outage discovered by phone).
16. Access rights: three roles — owner, editor, reader (a fourth existed but was never used).

Points 17–23 are verbatim repeats of 1–7 (staging, DB, login, logging, calendar, backups, API versioning); no new information.

Open for all 16 distinct decisions: ana assigns ownership at the Thursday meeting and it goes into the project notes.
